GEOMETRIC QUANTIZATION AND QUANTUM MOMENT MAPS ON
COADJOINT ORBITS AND K¨AHLER-EINSTEIN MANIFOLDS
NAICHUNG CONAN LEUNG, QIN LI, AND ZIMING NIKOLAS MA
Abstract. Deformation quantization and geometric quantization on K¨ahler manifolds give the
mathematical description of the algebra of quantum observables and the Hilbert spaces respectively,
where the later forms a representation of quantum observables asymptotically via Toeplitz operators.
When there is a Hamiltonian G-action on a K¨ahler manifold, there are associated symmetries on
both the quantum algebra and representation aspects. We show that in nice cases of coadjoint orbits
and K¨ahler-Einstein manifolds, these symmetries are strictly compatible (not only asymptotically).

A deformation quantization on a K¨ahler manifold X is called of Wick type (also known as separa-
tion of variables) if all the bi-diﬀerential operators Cl(f, g) take holomorphic and anti-holomorphic
derivatives of f and g respectively. It is shown in [14] that to every Wick type star product, there is
an associated closed formal (1, 1)-form −1
ℏω + α1 + α2ℏ+ α3ℏ2 + · · · known as the Karabegov form,
which gives rise to a one-one correspondence.
In [10], it is shown that there is a family of Fedosov connections induced from quantization of
L∞structure on K¨ahler manifolds, such that the formal closed (1, 1)-form −ω + Ωin equation (3.1)
is exactly the Karabegov form of the associated star product. The Berezin-Toeplitz quantization is
a Wick type deformation quantization whose Karabegov form is −1
ℏω −i · RicX. Since this formal

Abstract: Deformation quantization and geometric quantization on K¨ahler manifolds give the mathematical description of the algebra of quantum observables and the Hilbert spaces respectively, where the later forms a representation of quantum observables asymptotically via Toeplitz operators. When there is a Hamiltonian G-action on a K¨ahler manifold, there are associated symmetries on both the quantum algebra and representation aspects. We show that in nice cases of coadjoint orbits and K¨ahler-Einstein manifolds, these symmetries are strictly compatible (not only asymptotically).
